title: Monthly Outcome Ledger — week-by-week micro commitments & retrospective
content:
Purpose and framing:
- This doc is a writable ledger for the next 30 days. Focus: make 3 outcome bets for my area (runtime perf tooling) and convert those into weekly micro-commitments I can actually ship.
- Emphasis on evidence (PRs, perf curves, customer examples) and a quick confidence note after each week.

Top-level 30-day outcomes (one-sentence each):
1) Reduce 95th-percentile p99 latency on short-chat routes by ~10% via kernel selector tuning + smaller KV cache quick wins.
   - Success signal: p95/p99 graphs show sustained 8–12% drop for the target routes across a full day at 50% load.
2) Ship a lightweight batching knob in runtime that reduces token-costs for small bursts without increasing tail latency.
   - Success signal: 15% token-cost reduction on test harness with <3% increase in 99th latency.
3) Create a repeatable metric-checklist + eval harness for rolling out quantized model variants safely.
   - Success signal: checklist used in one internal rollout; at least one regression caught by the harness.

Weekly micro-commitments (concrete, 3–5 per week)
Week 1 (Feb 20–Feb 26): foundation + quick wins
- Review/annotate p99 trace samples for the top 6 slowish traces (2h).
- Prototype kernel-selector weights change in toy env (GH branch: GH-PR-1289).
- Add a heatmap export to perf dashboard to highlight short-chat routes (dashboard ticket: JIRA-RT-4921).
- Time-block: Tue/Wed 10:00–12:00 deep work; Reserve Fri 2–3pm for sync with Maya.
Confidence after week: 6/10 — early signs, blocked by telemetry gaps.

Week 2 (Feb 27–Mar 5): experiment + measure
- Run A/B run of kernel selector on 20% of traffic (canary) in staging for 48h.
- Implement micro-batching toggle (server-side switch) behind feature flag.
- Document measurement steps in the checklist draft and run one end-to-end test.
- Pair with Arjun on KV cache TTL experiments (30m pairing).
Confidence after week: 7/10 — canary shows signal but noise.

Week 3 (Mar 6–Mar 12): iterate + push to prod
- Rollout kernel-selection change to 60% with auto-rollback rule; monitor for regressions.
- Run cost simulation with micro-batching enabled vs baseline; write up results.
- Run eval harness on quantized-ops branch and capture top-3 drift metrics.
- Prep short demo for runtime team retro next week.
Confidence after week: 7.5/10 — cost sim promising; quantization drift needs follow-up.

Week 4 (Mar 13–Mar 19): stabilize + handoff
- Finalize checklist and add to infra-runbooks (owner: Maya for long-term upkeep).
- Post-mortem doc stub if rollout resurfaces issues.
- Wrap-up: PRs merged, dashboards annotated, handover notes to release-engineering.
Confidence target by end: 8.5/10.

Measurement heuristics (how I judge progress quickly)
- Primary metric: p99 latency on short-chat route (absolute ms).
- Secondary: token-cost-per-request (normalized), percent change in tail latency for burst windows.
- Tertiary: manual regressions flagged in eval harness (count), and qualitative customer-impact notes.
- Quick check cadence: daily p95/p99 snapshot (5–10min), weekly summary with 3 evidence bullets.

Mini-retro (notes captured during the month)
- What worked:
  - Small canaries + auto-rollback reduced my anxiety about pushing selector changes.
  - Time-blocking 2hrs twice-weekly helped produce uninterrupted experiment runs.
- What didn't:
  - Telemetry gaps (missing labels for route-level splits) delayed analysis ~2 days.
  - Multi-PR coordination overhead with infra team (slower than expected approvals).
- Root causes and mitigations:
  - Telemetry: add a minimal route-label shim in frontend proxy; file JIRA-OBS-211 for follow-up (ask SRE for quick assist).
  - Approvals: pre-schedule weekly 30m review with infra team; use draft PRs tagged with the related Jira key.

Open questions / risky assumptions
- Assumption: kernel-selector changes generalize across seq-length distributions. Risk: improvement only for short sequences, could regress medium-length. Mitigation: include stratified A/B by seq-length.
- Assumption: micro-batching knob won't meaningfully increase 99th latency under burst. Risk: queuing under load. Mitigation: conservative default, circuit-breaker rule in switch.

Evidence log (single-line references to artifacts)
- Feb 22: GH-PR-1289 — prototype kernel-selector tweaks (notes in PR).
- Feb 24: JIRA-RT-4921 — dashboard request; uploaded heatmap export.
- Mar 4: staging canary results (attach perf-csv in Confluence link).
- Mar 9: cost-sim table exported to sheet (link in linked_artifacts).

Quick wins backlog (if time)
- Add per-route sampling to traces to increase signal on short-chat spikes.
- Automate nightly perf-run so we have baseline snapshots every morning.
- Lightweight doc template for mini-retros used across eng-serving-runtime.

Personal operating promises (behavioral nudges)
- Keep weekly promises to max 5 items. If I have >5, I split into two weeks.
- Every Friday: 20-minute sprint-close to capture evidence & confidence score.
- Tag PRs with the week number and the primary outcome they serve.

Action items (next 72h)
- Finish GH-PR-1289 and request early review from Arjun.
- Add route-label shim to proxy (pair with SRE, JIRA-OBS-211).
- Create perf dashboard heatmap and link to this doc.

Free-form scratch (notes to self)
- If we can't get reliable p99 delta, pivot to cost-per-token as the leading KPI for this month.
- Remember: product teams care about perceived responsiveness; get a short clip to show product if numbers look good.
- Keep the checklist as "executable steps" not philosophy. One-liners are gold.

Finish note: this ledger is intentionally messy. The goal is fast feedback loops, not a perfect doc. I'll triage and convert stable parts into a playbook after the month.

— Isaac
